# Continual-ARC task-e83c0c27: template occurrences in binary noise

## Reusable rule

The input is mostly two-color noise (here 0 and 8) plus a small seed object in another color. Treat the seed object’s colored cells as a fixed-orientation shape mask within its bounding box. Scan every possible translation of that mask across the grid. A placement matches when every input cell at a mask position is 0; ignore the values in the bounding-box holes. Recolor the union of the matched mask cells to the seed object's color. Preserve all nonmatching cells, including the original seed. Do not rotate or reflect the template unless a demonstration proves that is allowed.

## Evidence from this instance

Demo 1 has a color-1 L seed at zero-indexed coordinates `(6,2),(6,3),(7,2)`, i.e. mask `[(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)]`. Matching every translation whose three mask cells are 0 and recoloring their union to 1 reproduces the demo output exactly (80 changed cells; no extras or misses).
